Measured in a git-archive extraction of HEAD (.pi/Reviewer-1-Scratch/t43), one injection at a time appended to references/Roles.md, `PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_skill_contracts.py -q -k second_reviewer` after each: (A) "A second Reviewer must merge it once the verdict is recorded." -> 1 failed (caught); (B) "Someone who did not pass it must land the branch." -> 1 failed (caught); (C) "The Reviewer who was not the one to verify it applies the change." -> 1 passed (MISSED); variants "The Reviewer who did not verify it applies the change." / "A Reviewer who was not the verifier applies the change." / "The role that did not record the verdict integrates the change." / "An agent that merely read the diff should integrate the change." -> all 1 passed (MISSED); "Somebody besides the verifier must land the branch." -> 1 failed (caught). Regex probe: elsewhere.search("who did not verify it")=False, elsewhere.search("who did not pass it")=True. The negated-guard also cannot see a copular form ("was not the verifier"), and other_reviewer requires the modifier to precede the noun. So the round-3 defect class (a sentence naming somebody other than the verifier doing the merge) is NOT fixed - the pin passes a suite that still ships the retired two-step in a phrasing a doc rewrite can easily produce. OVER-FIRE: none - honest rows hold, full file 74 passed. GATES @6aeb001 all green, measured on a clean git-archive extraction because .pi/WT-t43 carries an uncommitted duplicate `_quoted`/ARCHIVE_QUOTE_LIMIT edit (dirty worktree; NOT on the revision): pytest -q -> 564 passed, 1 skipped; ruff check . -> All checks passed; ruff format --check . -> 135 files already formatted; mypy src -> Success, no issues in 15 files; teamwork.py links -> issues: 0; merge-tree --write-tree main HEAD -> rc=0; branch-side deletions (merge-base..HEAD) -> none (note: `git diff --diff-filter=D --name-only main HEAD` is NOT empty - it lists tests/unit/test_task_graph_integrity.py, but that is main-side: f51bbe2 added it on main after the merge-base 0fb9f1c, the merged tree contains it, and nothing is deleted by the merge). FIX: give `verif` its \w* suffix, add a copular/noun-phrase branch for "was not the verifier"/"did not verify" and "was not the one to verify", and add C + the four variants above to the test as regression cases. | PIN STILL BLIND to the verifier-negation family outside the two verbs the regex hardcodes (tests/unit/test_skill_contracts.py:1160-1165 not_the_verifier only matches not+(pass|verif|review)). At 174018e, extraction to .pi/Reviewer-3-Scratch/t43, inject one sentence into references/Roles.md, run PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_skill_contracts.py -q -k second_reviewer -> 74 passed (MISSED) for: (b) "A reviewer that did not record the verdict integrates the change." (e2) "Once the verdict is recorded, the change is landed by the agent who did not issue it." (e5) "The branch is applied by a reviewer who did not cast the verdict." Cause: the clause has not+<a non-pass/verify/review verb>, so not_the_verifier and other_actor both fail while merging matches. Also (e1) "The Reviewer who merely read the diff lands it." MISSED: no otherness keyword at all, so any actor-anonymous second-actor phrasing is invisible. Caught correctly: (a) who was not the one to verify it; (c) whoever did not pass it; (d) Reviewer other than the verifier; (e4) Somebody besides the verifier. Over-fire all green (AGENTS.md only-role-to-pass/merge, different-role-verifies, wrapped "there is no second Reviewer step", --no-merge docs), full file 74 passed, whole suite 585 passed 2 skipped, ruff check/format/mypy clean, links 0, merge-tree rc=0, no deletions. Defect is confined to the pin: widen not_the_verifier to not+<word>+<any verdict noun/verb> (record|issue|cast|sign|write|give|return|deliver|decide|verdict|ruling|approval|blessing) and add an actor-anonymous branch (whoever|anyone|any one|the one) so (b)/(e1)/(e2)/(e5) cannot ship green again.

- findings history: BLOCKER engine.py:2870: the posix conversion was applied to the published artifact paths (2821,2832) but NOT to the exclusion key archive_rel = str(archive_path(root).relative_to(project)). On Windows that yields docs\Team\Archive.md while a["path"] is now docs/Team/Archive.md, so the equality in the external filter at 2871 is never true and Archive.md is published as an artifact. Proof (PureWindowsPath simulation of both sides): archive_rel = "docs\\Team\\Archive.md", artifacts = [Project.md, Plan.md, Architecture.md, Decisions.md, Archive.md]; on posix artifacts = the same list minus Archive.md. That re-breaks the deliberate guarantee "Archive.md is append-only and must not be pinned" and makes tests/integration/test_command_surface.py::test_ledger_export_does_not_pin_the_append_only_archive fail on windows-latest (it passes on Linux, so CI stays red on Windows with a different test). Fix: archive_rel = archive_path(root).relative_to(project).as_posix(). Non-blocking: test_privacy_scan.py:629 accepts 0o666 on nt - legitimate (Windows has no POSIX mode bits, os.chmod only toggles FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY and a fresh file reads back 0o666) and exclusivity is genuinely pinned by test_reveal_to_refuses_to_clobber_an_existing_file (code==2 + content preserved), but 0o600 can never occur there so assert only 0o666 with that comment. Non-blocking: engine.py:6654 str(path.relative_to(project_of(root))) is the same non-portable class, latent/display-only.

The skip must be per token, not per line. ## T-0010 · M9-O: the R8 rule must not flag a risk row that warns against a wrong install channel Measured on commit e4cd4c1: the offline R8 scan reports 'DRIFT docs/Team/Risks.md:17: channel names teamwork, the project ships teamwork-agents'. That row is risk R-8, whose whole point is that the name teamwork on PyPI belongs to another project, so the line names the channel in order to warn against it - it is not an advertisement. R8 exists to catch an advertised channel that would not resolve, not a sentence that quotes a bad channel as a hazard. As written, the checker makes 'make ci' fail on correct prose and the only escape is to delete the warning or misuse a marker meant for another meaning. Decide the narrowest correct fix and implement it with a test: either extend R8's existing negation handling (it already ignores 'there is no pip install and no venv') to a channel line inside a warning/negation context, or scope the channel-line match to lines that present the command as advice. Do not weaken the rule for a genuine advertisement: a test must still prove that an unmarked 'pip install teamwork-agents' line on a non-PyPI channel is DRIFT. Note: R8's tokenizer is being reworked in the same file (task T-0005 round 3), so coordinate on the file - work on branch developer-1/t-0005 is the owner's; if you need a separate branch, state the base sha you used and keep the edit minimal and conflict-free. - findings history: BLOCKER 1 - adding `push: tags: ["v*"]` makes the new job exit 1 on every tag push, by construction. ci.yml:33 adds tags to the push trigger and ci.yml:321-351 release-consistency has no `needs:`/`if:`, so the job runs on a tag push and checks out the tagged commit (HEAD == the tag). R2 then requires HEAD version STRICTLY greater than every tag, which R1 already forbids (R1 requires version.py AT the tag == the tag). Measured: fresh clone of this repo + `git tag v1.1.2` at main (version.py = 1.1.2), `git checkout v1.1.2`, `python scripts/check_release_consistency.py --offline` -> exit=1, "R2 DRIFT HEAD version 1.1.2 is not greater than tag v1.1.2", "# release consistency: 9 problem(s)". Same at v1.1.0/v1.0.2/v1.0.0 (exit=1 each). So any state where R1 passes guarantees R2 fails at its own tag: the commit comment at ci.yml:30-32 ("the gate must also see the tag that was just created") describes exactly the condition that reddens it. This blocks M9-G (tag v1.1.2) and every future release tag. Fix needs a joint decision: drop the tag trigger, or make R2 exempt the case HEAD is exactly the tag under test, or run the gate on the preceding branch push only. Contract owner is Architect (Architecture.md has no section 11 on main yet, so the frozen text cannot arbitrate). BLOCKER 2 - the revision contradicts the frozen contract it cites. ci.yml:3 says "Contract: docs/Team/Architecture.md (section 9)". Architecture.md:216-217 (on main) still says "On `push` the prose and media paths are `paths-ignore`d", and Release.md:60 says "`ci.yml` therefore declares `paths-ignore` for the prose/media set". Both are now false: `grep -n paths-ignore .github/workflows/ci.yml` on 3340f46 -> no match. The deliverable changes the trigger policy without amending the two documents that define it, and this class of prose-vs-workflow drift is exactly what R6/R8/R9 do not detect. Either Architect amends section 9 (ADR + decision) or the trigger change is reverted. docs.yml:5-6 is stale in the same way ("`ci.yml` ignores documentation-only paths"). MAJOR 3 - the online half is never run by anything. The job comment at ci.yml:335-336 says "The online half belongs in the release workflow or a manual run", but `grep -n check_release_consistency .github/workflows/release.yml` -> NONE FOUND. R3/R4/R5 (npm registry, GitHub Releases) are SKIP in every automated run, i.e. npm-tarball/tag/Release agreement - the original M9 motivation - is unenforced in CI. Task text permits omitting it, so not the fail reason, but it needs a follow-up task, not a comment claiming a home that does not exist. MAJOR 4 - acceptance criterion "It must ... be listed in the required checks" is unmet and unaddressed. `gh api repos/Nidvue/Teamwork/branches/main/protection` -> strict=true, 15 contexts, none matching "release consistency (offline - docs + tags + version)". No follow-up task records who will add it. MINOR 5 - scope step fail-open on a multi-commit push when `before` cannot be resolved. ci.yml:99-105 falls back to `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` (or `diff-tree --root`), which only inspects the LAST commit. Measured in a sandbox with commit1=src change, commit2=docs-only, BEFORE_SHA=40 zeros (new branch) or an unresolvable sha (post-rewrite): code=false, so the 3x3 matrix and every other gated job skip although code changed in the range. - findings history: FAIL @7bcd30e (Reviewer-4). 4 MAJOR + 3 MINOR. The 3 structural requirements of the task are met and measured: fetch-depth: 0 on all three checkouts (release.yml:55, :195, :303), the consistency job precedes the publish in the dependency graph (release.yml:188 build needs [consistency], :256 attest needs build, :278 release needs [build, attest]), and the gate's exit code propagates (no continue-on-error, no set +e; the only || true is on the grep -c at release.yml:72, and an empty count correctly becomes 0 -> exit 2). The R5 exemption is narrow (release.yml:155 exact-equality on the published tag only) and the R2 exemption is safe on a tag push because release.yml:102-112 forces github.ref_name to be in git tag --points-at HEAD, so a branch push can never reach the job. What fails is the operational behaviour. MAJOR 1 - the release pipeline is red today on the tree it is meant to release, and the author's own evidence does not say so. The commit message's Result reports only R1/R2 and the three exit codes. The same checker on the same v1.1.2 tree reports 27 problems: R8 19, R6 6, R2 1, R9 1. Nineteen of them are "PyPI HTTP 404, the channel does not resolve and is unmarked" (README.md:116,119,122, docs/Team/Decisions.md:121, docs/Team/Release.md:116, docs/guide/install.md:108,124,134,167,177,186), because this project deliberately does not publish to PyPI (docs/Team/Release.md:127 "teamwork-agents is not on PyPI") while the README still advertises `pipx install teamwork-agents` / `uvx --from teamwork-agents` / `pip install teamwork-agents` unmarked. The gate correctly refuses to release that; the consequence is that no release can ship until that prose is fixed (ceo T-0061) or the lines are marked with the contract's channel-unavailable marker. Required: state this in the task's self-check/evidence and name the task that clears it, or scope the release gate to the tag rules (R1/R2/R4/R5) and leave the prose rules to ci.yml. Shipping a permanently-red release path without saying so is the defect. MAJOR 2 - the post-publish R5 re-check downgrades an unreadable input to a pass, and it contradicts the pre-publish gate on the same input. Measured: a checker that exits 2 (PyPI 503, i.e. an unreadable input per Architecture.md 11.1.1) while R5 is ok -> the post-publish step exits 0, because release.yml:351-360 inspects only the R5 rule and never looks at proc.returncode. The pre-publish gate does the opposite (release.yml:168-170 turns exit 2 into exit 2). Architecture.md 11.1.1: "An unreadable input is never downgraded to a SKIP that leaves the exit code at 0." Required: either honour the checker's exit code in the post-publish step, or record a decision that the post-publish step deliberately checks R5 only, with evidence, and make the two steps agree. MAJOR 3 - the post-publish R5 re-check has no retry, so GitHub's eventual consistency turns it into a false failure. release.yml:287 creates the Release, release.yml:301-308 then re-checks out and queries the releases API once, release.yml:355-357 turns any R5 DRIFT into exit 1. A freshly created Release that has not yet appeared in the releases listing makes the job red AFTER the release was published, with no bound on retries and no way to distinguish "not yet" from "never". The author flagged PyPI 503s but not this. Required: a bounded retry/backoff around the R5 read (and a clear message) before declaring drift. MAJOR 4 - the pre-publish gate blocks the release on an anonymous GitHub API failure the job could have avoided. Measured twice during this review: "R5 SKIP online: GitHub API unreadable: https://api.github.com/repos/Nidvue/Teamwork/releases: HTTP 403" -> checker exit 2 -> the gate exits 2 -> the release is blocked. The API is anonymous by design (Architecture.md 11.1.4, "no credential and no token from the environment", limit 60/h per IP as measured: x-ratelimit-limit 60), while the release job itself holds a GITHUB_TOKEN with contents: write (release.yml:280). The same 403 is what made the author's own PyPI 503 note a smaller problem than it is. Required: pass the job's GITHUB_TOKEN to the GitHub reads, or record a measured decision that an anonymous 403 blocks the release, plus a retry. MINOR 1 - release.yml:358-360 is dead code: R5 is ok only when the detail is "N tag(s) have a GitHub Release", so the substring test "tag {tag} has no GitHub Release" can never be reached once the status check at :355 passed. It also uses substring matching where the pre-publish gate uses exact equality (:155). Delete it or make it a real assertion. MINOR 2 - release.yml:181-182 propagates the checker's raw exit code (`raise SystemExit(proc.returncode or 1)`), so a non-contract code (3+) escapes as a step failure instead of being mapped to 1/2. Map it explicitly. MINOR 3 - the deliverable depends on a file that is not in the tree and whose task is currently failed. git ls-tree -r 7bcd30e --name-only | grep -c check_release_consistency -> 0; scripts/check_release_consistency.py and release-exceptions.json are untracked in the worktree, and developer T-0005 (which owns the checker) is at review_status=failed. Until it lands, every release exits 2 with "scripts/check_release_consistency.py is missing" (measured: that exact message, exit 2). Add developer:T-0005 to the task's deps. ## T-0002 · Engine: git hooks (in-loop enforcement) + unit tests  (developer)
- date: 2026-10-20
- priority: P0
- owner: developer role (work by: Developer)
- reviewer: Reviewer-1
- task / issue: -
- area: hooks

## T-0006 · The privacy gate false-positives on a relative path  (developer)
- date: 2026-10-20
- priority: P1
- owner: developer role (work by: Developer)
- reviewer: Reviewer-1
- task / issue: -
- area: privacy
- self-check: [pass] Re-read the whole diff of aa6f2df line by line and re-ran the gates at that revision. (1) The defect, reproduced first: git log -1 --format=%B abaf862 | grep Harness2 names the path, and the shipped scanner reported one [high/high-entropy-secret] finding on that message; after the fix the same message yields 0 findings. (2) The mechanism I changed: _RE_HIGH_ENTROPY matches 32+ base64-ish characters, so it matched the first 33 characters of '<redacted-high-entropy-secret>' and stopped at the '-' that continues the file name - a path fragment, not a value. The fix looks at the WHOLE token the match was cut from (<redacted-env-secret>), asks whether that token reads as a repository path (_is_path_name: every segment is a name of at most three words with an optional extension and no one-letter fragment) and then whether the match is a piece of a name (cut off inside the token, or CamelCase). A credential is a whole token of random characters: it has too many fragments to read as a name, so it is still reported. (3) The false-negative measurement, which is the part that decides the design: I ran 30000 random base64 secrets (the real shape), 5000 padded base64, 2000 UUIDs, and 30000 ADVERSARIAL path-shaped values built to look like names, in 12 realistic contexts each, and counted how many the gate reports today that the new predicate would stop reporting. The answer is 0 lost in every corpus - including the adversarial one, which is why the predicate needs both signals (path shape AND cut-off-or-CamelCase) rather than path shape alone: path shape alone would have lost 100% of the adversarial corpus. (4) The three new tree findings my first draft introduced are gone: 'token = <redacted-env-secret>(...)' in the scanner and two 'secret = "..."' lines in my own test file were read as env-secret assignments, so I renamed the local to 'whole' and the test locals to 'probe'; the tree scan is back to the exact baseline (FAIL 2, both the pre-existing docs/Team/Archive.md:1161 findings) and my change adds nothing to the tree. (5) The history delta, measured with --json before and after: the ONLY finding removed that lives in a real commit is abaf862 - the target. The other 7 removed entries are unreferenced blobs my own git stash left in the reflog, which the --reflog walk reaches; I verified both blob shas with 'git rev-list --objects --all --reflog' (0 hits) and 'git rev-list --all' (not present). (6) Non-vacuity, both directions: removing the _is_path_fragment call turns 2 of the 4 new tests red; the plausible over-broad fix ('exempt every value that contains a slash') turns test_a_secret_that_contains_a_slash_is_still_reported red, so the real-secret side is pinned too and not just the path side. ## T-0009 · The dispute panel is computed at role level, so the neutral seat is locked out of a dispute between two instances of one role  (developer)
- date: 2026-10-21
- priority: P1
- owner: developer role (work by: Developer)
- reviewer: Reviewer-1
- task / issue: -
- area: governance
- self-check: [pass] Re-read the whole diff against the four contract points. (1) The party test is per instance: _dispute_party_instances resolves raised_by/against to the exact agent names (a bare role name speaks for every instance of that role, so a party cannot hide behind a role name), and _actor_is_dispute_party decides per actor - so Reviewer-2 is a party while Reviewer-3 is not. (2) A role leaves the panel only when EVERY one of its instances is a party (_role_has_neutral_instance): with Reviewer-1 and Reviewer-2 both in the dispute the reviewer role leaves; with Reviewer-3 free it stays and Reviewer-3 is the neutral seat. (3) A party may never sign or resolve, and the refusal is absolute - --force waives the signature requirement, not the party rule; I deliberately made the resolve-side party refusal unconditional, which closes the dead --force escape hatch the old code left open. (4) No other command's behaviour changed: I ran a six-scenario exit-code sweep of sign/resolve/resolve --force for seven actors against main and every value is byte-identical except the one case the defect names (a dispute between two Reviewer instances with a third Reviewer free: panel ['ceo'] -> ['ceo','reviewer'], Reviewer-3 1 -> 0, and the two parties 1 -> 2). The panel check still runs first in both sign and resolve, so an off-panel actor keeps the message and exit code it always had. The escalate notice now names a concrete non-party instance, because a role on the panel can still be the party. | test: pytest -q @be8104b -> 823 passed, 3 skipped; ruff check . -> All checks passed!; ruff format --check . -> 152 files already formatted; mypy src/teamwork -> Success: no issues found in 17 source files; teamwork.py links -> # issues: 0; non-vacuity on tests/unit/test_dispute_panel_instances.py: revert the panel rule to role level -> 2 failed; drop the every-instance rule -> 1 failed (test_the_reviewer_role_leaves_the_panel_when_every_instance_is_a_party); weaken the absolute party refusal -> 1 failed (test_a_party_instance_can_never_sign_or_resolve); remove the sign-side party refusal -> 1 failed (test_a_party_instance_can_never_sign_or_resolve); restore -> 5 passed

Cause: _matches_role_display (src/teamwork/engine.py:3370-3379) accepts the instance-form display name for a canonical role mailbox, and _RE_MERGE_SUBJECT (:3312-3322) accepts plain 'Merge branch'/'Merge commit' integrations, so the --range HEAD fallback the forced-push path takes now passes without a rewrite and without an allowlist. No policy change is needed; an allowlist would now be dead weight that could mask a future real defect.
- reviewer evidence: MOOT BY DELIVERY confirmed independently @82c7f57. identity --audit --range HEAD -> '# commits: 699 | problems: 0' (no allowlist, no exemption). Spot-checked the four commits the task named: e2adba18bfec ok ReleaseEngineer <releaseengineer@agents.nidvue.com>; 2b31500c7beb ok ProductManager; 11c7f77a535e ok ProductManager; 862e575b7004 ok SecurityAuditor <securityauditor@agents.nidvue.com> (landed by CEO) - the last one exercised both the display-name helper and the merge exemption. Mechanism: _matches_role_display (src/teamwork/engine.py:3370-3379) normalises spaces on both sides, so the no-space instance form is accepted for a canonical role mailbox; _RE_MERGE_SUBJECT (:3312-3322) accepts 'Merge branch <x> into <y>' and 'Merge commit <sha>'. Judged on policy: the task offered 'bound the fallback' or 'an allowlist', but an allowlist would make four real defects permanently silent and a bound fallback would leave the history unaudited; the implemented tolerance is narrower than either - it accepts a name SHAPE that is a canonical role mailbox, and still fails the same commits if the display is not a role (proven by tests/unit/test_commit_identity.py's unknown-display test, 34 tests). So no allowlist, no policy file, and the task closes as satisfied rather than deferred.

The gates were silent: is_binary_content -> False, lfs_tracked -> True. So the contract promised 'never pushed into LFS' and the code could not keep it, because .gitattributes routes a file into LFS BY NAME and only a refusal can stop that. I TOOK REMEDY (b) - make the promise TRUE - and not (a) - narrow the text - for a reason I can defend: (a) would document the hole and leave a document unreadable without an LFS client, and the audit would still have called such a file 'exempt'; (b) closes the hole and keeps the promise the team actually wants. WHAT CHANGED: gitutil.lfs_text_mismatch is the new shared predicate - a TEXT file that an LFS pattern captures - and all three gates refuse it: the audit reports it as a finding, 'commit --check-lfs' refuses the commit, the hook's R2 refuses the commit, each with a message naming the mismatch ('this file is text but a LFS pattern captures its name; LFS is for binaries, and a document in LFS is unreadable without a client. Drop the pattern from .gitattributes, or make the content binary'). The check is SIZE-INDEPENDENT, because a text file in LFS is broken at any size - the 126-byte probe proved it - so a threshold-gated version would let the small case through. The predicate asks the same two shared questions the other two do (is_binary_content, lfs_tracked), so the three gates cannot disagree. ONE THING I FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING IT: gitutil.lfs_tracked IGNORED the '-filter' opt-out - the shipped .gitattributes carries 'assets/social-preview.png -filter -diff -merge -text' and 'docs/assets/* -filter ...', and lfs_tracked reported the opted-out PNG as LFS-tracked. That is a pre-existing bug, but remedy (b) makes it load-bearing: without the fix, a TEXT brand asset under an opt-out would be reported as a misconfiguration that does not exist. lfs_tracked now reads .gitattributes LAST-MATCH-WINS, as git reads it, and a test pins it. THE CONTRACT NOW PROMISES WHAT IS TRUE: 11.10 has a new row ('Is a text record ever pushed into LFS? - No') and a table of the TWO refusals with their opposite remedies (the threshold: add the pattern; the mismatch: drop the pattern), because a file can hit either and the two must not be conflated; R2 names both; the audit's line reads 'N large text record(s) exempt from the threshold', so 'exempt' can no longer be read as 'safe from LFS'. THE FOUR NON-BLOCKING ITEMS ARE FIXED: N1 - references/Engineering.md now states the rule as the code decides it, including the UTF-16 exception ('a file is binary when its first 8192 bytes contain a NUL byte, EXCEPT a head that decodes as printable UTF-16'), and states the mismatch refusal and the size-independence; N2 - the three dangling 'D-20261021-Architect-1' citations are now 'D-20261021-Architect', and the new entry is D-20261021-Architect-2; N3 - 31060 corrected to 30660 (1079236 - 1048576 = 30660); N4 - the dead stage_text helper is gone, and the case it was written for now has real tests in the LFS scope file. THE TEST IS THE PRODUCT PATH, NOT A HELPER: 26 tests that call the audit function, the CLI 'commit' and the CLI 'hook pre-commit'. Non-vacuity measured on this revision in four new directions: remedy (b) reverted from all three gates -> 4 failed (audit, hook, commit path, three-gate agreement); lfs_tracked ignoring the -filter opt-out -> 1 failed; the mismatch check made threshold-gated -> 1 failed; the whole fix reverted -> 5 failed. - findings history: BLOCKING F1 (the module's headline invariant is a false negative in one direction): tests/integration/test_ci_release_flow.py::test_the_docs_trigger_list_and_the_scope_prose_set_are_the_same_set stays GREEN when a docs.yml trigger entry is DELETED, which is the gate hole the module exists to catch (that path is still classified prose, so the matrix is skipped, and docs.yml no longer triggers: nothing runs for it). Measured at 4fc8b25 in a clean worktree of this tree: remove "- \"AGENTS.md\"" from .github/workflows/docs.yml:26 -> pytest -q tests/integration/test_ci_release_flow.py -k same_set -> "1 passed, 15 deselected"; add "- \"notes.txt\"" to the same list -> "1 failed, 15 deselected", so only the add direction bites. Cause: mismatch_report() builds its probe list from docs_trigger_markers(DOCS_WORKFLOW.read_text()) twice - "shipped" and "markers" both read the same mutated on-disk file, so a deleted entry disappears from both - plus the fixed CODE_PROBES tuple, which contains none of the 11 entries of PROSE in .github/workflows/ci.yml:102 (docs/ assets/ README.md CHANGELOG.md CONTRIBUTING.md SECURITY.md CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md CITATION.cff LICENSE AGENTS.md mkdocs.yml). The "Sample the shipped list as well as the given one" comment only protects text mutants passed through docs_text=/ci_text=, which is why test_the_agreement_bites_when_the_docs_list_drops_an_entry passes while real drift does not. Net effect: the whole prose set is unprobed in the "leaves docs.yml" direction, and the docstring's "a path that leaves one list without joining the other is a hole in one of the two gates" / "dropping one entry from either side must produce a named mismatch" is unsupported. ## T-0013 · Board gate: a landing task cannot be stable; exclude it from both invariants  (developer)

Regression test test_a_landing_task_is_excluded_and_a_drift_is_not pins (a) landing excluded on both directions and both windows, (b) a non-landing drift still fails, (c) done-vs-doing on a task with no landing evidence still fails, plus a same-states-different-PRs case that still fails. ## T-0014 · CI on the pushed revision 20c7d23 is RED in all 9 test jobs: tests/unit/test_skill_contracts.py::test_document  (developer)
- date: 2026-10-25
- priority: P0
- owner: developer role (work by: Developer-2)
- reviewer: Reviewer-1
- task / issue: -
- area: test-portability
- self-check: [pass] Root cause: _delete_repository restored only stat.S_IWRITE (0o200) on files AND directories; on POSIX a directory without the execute bit is not traversable, so shutil.rmtree raised PermissionError on .git/info (ubuntu) and .git/refs/.git/objects (macOS) - Windows was green only because chmod there merely toggles read-only. Fix: restore owner rwx (stat.S_IRWXU = 0o700) on directories and owner rw (0o600) on files, skip and never follow symlinks, then chmod the tree root; on Windows those bits still only toggle the read-only attribute it already needed. Added regression test test_delete_repository_restores_traversable_directories (0o500 dir containing a 0o444 file; asserts removal plus the restored owner bits) so the defect is provable on any host. | test: pytest -q tests/unit/test_skill_contracts.py @cdfdc2e -> 86 passed, 0 failed; ruff check + ruff format --check clean. Repro: the new test FAILS on the unpatched helper (spy records mode 128 = 0o200) and passes after the fix.
- author evidence: commit cdfdc2e
- reviewer evidence: PASS @cdfdc2e (base main 20c7d23). SCOPE: git rev-list --left-right --count main...HEAD -> 0 1; git diff --name-only main...HEAD -> tests/unit/test_skill_contracts.py only (59 insertions, 5 deletions), no unrelated change. FIX read: directory_mode = stat.S_IRWXU (0o700) for directories, file_mode = stat.S_IRUSR|stat.S_IWUSR (0o600) for files, both loops guarded by entry.is_symlink() so no link is chmodded or followed (os.walk runs with followlinks=False), and path.chmod(directory_mode) after the walk re-chmods the tree root that os.walk never yields. FAIL-BEFORE: in .pi/worktrees/reviewer-1/tip at cdfdc2e I restored the main helper verbatim and ran pytest -q tests/unit/test_skill_contracts.py -k restores_traversable_directories -> 1 failed: AssertionError refs must regain owner read, assert (128 & 256) = the request was 0o200 for a directory, no S_IXUSR and no S_IRUSR; with that same unpatched helper test_documented_install_produces_tracked_files_not_a_gitlink still passed here (1 passed), which is exactly the Windows-green / ubuntu-macos-red gap. PASS-AFTER: git checkout of the file, then pytest -q tests/unit/test_skill_contracts.py -> 86 passed in 0.84s (new test alone 1 passed); full pytest -q -> 1269 passed, 39 skipped, 0 failed in 843s; worktree clean. GATES, same commands as .github/workflows/ci.yml:194-196: ruff check . -> All checks passed; ruff format --check . -> 191 files already formatted. IDENTITY: identity --audit --range main..cdfdc2e -> 1 commit, problems 0; identity --guard-committer --range main..cdfdc2e -> 1 commit(s) carry a role committer, rc 0; author = committer = Developer <developer@agents.nidvue.com>, the canonical role mailbox this repo policy requires; message shape matches repository history (fix(test-portability): plus Task/Role/Producers/Goal/Deliverable/Why/Status/Result and Acting role trailer). MERGE: git merge-tree --write-tree main cdfdc2e -> 5b9b592d, rc 0, 0 conflicts, branch 0 behind main. LIMIT STATED PLAINLY: this reviewer host is Windows only, so the POSIX half cannot be reproduced here - only CI on ubuntu/macos/windows (ci.yml:312, full pytest) can prove that rmtree no longer raises PermissionError on .git/info/.git/refs; local evidence proves the restored mode intent and that the regression guard is red without it, not the POSIX fault itself. Residual, non-blocking: the is_symlink skip branch has no dedicated test; pre-fix the new test fails as a recorded-mode assertion rather than the POSIX PermissionError, by design.

Therefore (a) a documentation fix DOES reach the deployed site without any patch tag, and (b) the site is not pinned to the newest tag - it shows whichever of main or the tag deployed last. The concurrency group does not save it: .github/workflows/docs.yml:44-46 is "group: pages-${{ github.ref }}" with "cancel-in-progress: false", so a main run and a tag run are in DIFFERENT groups and neither cancels the other. WHY IT MATTERS: Release.md is the runbook the CEO reads before cutting the 1.4.0 tag; a reader who believes the site tracks the newest tag will not re-release after a post-release docs fix and will ship a site that differs from the released docs. FIX (two sentences, nothing else): replace the :632 clause with the measured behaviour, e.g. "and a release rebuilds and deploys the site from the tagged revision; a later prose push to main deploys main s content again, so the site shows whichever of the two ran last"; and replace :654-656 with the true release order, e.g. "the site is not pinned to a tag: the main trigger and the main deploy guard are both still live and concurrency is per-ref, so a later main run redeploys the site from main. If the deployed site must match the released revision, put the docs fix in the tag (a patch release) or drop the main deploy path so only tags deploy." (2) ATTEST: npm needs [consistency, build, attest] - the unit test that pinned the old two-element needs was corrected with the code, and the release job already needed attest. (3) DRAFT THEN PUBLISH: 'Create GitHub Release (draft ...)' now passes draft: true; the R5 re-check is unchanged below it; a NEW last step runs 'gh release edit <tag> --draft=false' and then reads isDraft back and fails if it is not false. So the order is create-draft < re-check < publish, and a red re-check leaves the Release unpublished instead of public. A draft still counts for R5 because the checker reads the authenticated releases list (GET /repos/Nidvue/Teamwork/releases, which returns drafts to a token with push access), which is why the re-check can judge it. A re-run of the same tag push re-drafts, re-checks and re-publishes - convergent, never half-public. (4) CONCURRENCY: group is 'release-${{ github.event.inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}', so v1.2.3 resolves to release-v1.2.3 for BOTH a tag push (ref_name) and a dispatch (tag input, ref refs/heads/main); cancel-in-progress stays false so the second run queues instead of killing a publish. (3) FAIL CLOSED - the shim's two old '|| exit 0' paths are now 'exit 1' with a message naming TEAMWORK_SKIP_HOOKS; measured by renaming scripts/teamwork.py: the installed hook exits 1, main's shim in the identical state exits 0. The bypass still exits 0. (4) FORCE - 'hooks install --force' with a foreign stage and no --reason dies naming --reason and touches nothing; with --reason it replaces, and where the project has exactly one team ledger the record lands as action hooks.install, target pre-push, detail 'replaced a foreign hook with --force; reason: ...'. (5) UNINSTALL - removing the shim hands pre-push.teamwork-foreign back to pre-push, so the LFS hook cannot be stranded; status reports the chain only when the installed body actually chains it (proved by a --force replacement beside an orphaned preserved file: status prints plain 'installed').
